title: Start of the Late Window for Lienholder Releases
content:
**Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda — dating rule for refunds released to the lienholder**

The late window of a refund released to the lienholder is the period from whose start the refund payment period, and any late days after it, are counted. Its start depends on the signed request the release reads, which is the waiver's completed cancellation request: its stated reason, the date the holder signed it, and the date it was recorded. Whether the waiver's purchase deal stands unwound, and the date it was unwound, are read from the Vehicle Purchase Agreements records (the deal's status and its closed date).

## Where the late window starts

1. Where the signed request states the reason deal unwound and the waiver's purchase deal stands unwound, the late window starts on that deal's closed date, the date it was unwound.
2. Where the signed request states the reason customer request and was recorded more than 7 calendar days after the holder signed it, the late window starts on the signed request date.
3. In every other case the late window starts on the effective date of the cancellation, which is the waiver's closing date (or the release date where the waiver carries none).

## Reading the 7-day test

Days are counted from the signed request date (day 0) to the date the request was recorded.

| Reason on the request | Recorded after signing | Late window starts on |
|---|---|---|
| Customer request | 8 days or more | The signed request date |
| Customer request | 7 days or fewer | The effective date of the cancellation |
| Deal unwound, deal stands unwound | any | The deal's unwind date |
| Deal unwound, deal not unwound | any | The effective date of the cancellation |

## Timeline cases (hypothetical dates)

- A holder signs a customer-request cancellation on Day 0; it is recorded on Day 9 and the waiver closes on Day 9. The window starts on Day 0.
- The same request recorded on Day 7 leaves the window at the closing date, Day 7.
- A deal-unwound request on a deal unwound on Day 2, with the waiver closing on Day 5, starts the window on Day 2.
